questions.q: Which two selves does the summary say influence your actions?
a: A conscious self and an automatic self
A rational self and an emotional self
An inner child and an adult self
A public self and a private self
questions.why: Lesson 1 says we have a conscious self that reasons and an automatic self that runs when we act out of habit.

questions.q: When does the automatic self usually take over?
a: When you act out a bad habit without thinking
When you carefully weigh a decision
When you plan your week in advance
When you meditate on your breath
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that bad habits happen automatically, since no one would choose them consciously.

questions.q: What does the summary say happens when you repress your emotions?
a: They build up and eventually push you toward self-destructive acts
They disappear completely once you ignore them
They make you calmer and more rational over time
They only affect people with serious addictions
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares emotions to water in an overflowing tub and says they will find a way out.

questions.q: How does the summary recommend training your mindfulness?
a: Sitting daily and returning your attention to your breath
Writing down every bad habit you notice
Avoiding all thoughts during a long walk
Repeating affirmations before you sleep
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends 30 minutes a day of focusing and re-focusing on the breath to notice habits before they start.

questions.q: What does the summary say about the fake it till you make it approach?
a: Keep trying after a relapse instead of berating yourself
Pretend to be cured so others stop worrying
Avoid social situations where you might slip
Wait until you feel ready before making changes
questions.why: Lesson 3 says beating yourself up after a slip sabotages progress, so you should keep going until the new habit sticks.
